headline: Journalist Iqbal Sobhan arrested on murder charges linked to July protests
summary: The former information advisor to ousted PM Sheikh Hasina was detained from the DBC News office in Dhaka.
details: Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury, a journalist and former information advisor to ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has been formally placed under arrest.
He was detained by police detectives from the offices of private broadcaster DBC in Dhaka’s Mohakhali on Wednesday afternoon.
The arrest is in connection with a murder case filed at Jatrabari Police Station related to the Anti-discrimination Student Movement protests.
DBC News Special Correspondent Rajib Ghosh, who was detained alongside Sobhan, has been released after signing a bond.
The update was confirmed by Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Detective Branch (DB) chief Shafiqul Islam early Thursday morning.
caption:
A former advisor to Sheikh Hasina has been arrested on murder charges. Who is Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury?

Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury, a journalist and former information advisor to ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has been formally placed under arrest.

He was detained by police detectives from the offices of private broadcaster DBC in Dhaka’s Mohakhali on Wednesday afternoon.

The arrest is in connection with a murder case filed at Jatrabari Police Station related to the Anti-discrimination Student Movement protests.

DBC News Special Correspondent Rajib Ghosh, who was detained alongside Sobhan, has been released after signing a bond.

The update was confirmed by Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Detective Branch (DB) chief Shafiqul Islam early Thursday morning.

topic: two killed in teknaf over yaba dispute
headline_marked: Drug dispute: [[2 killed in Teknaf]] over yaba consignment
headline: Drug dispute: 2 killed in Teknaf over yaba consignment
summary: Two men were beaten to death in the hills of Cox's Bazar over a dispute involving a hijacked drug consignment, police said.
details: Two men, identified as Moktar Kamal (48) and Ali Akbar (30), were killed and two others injured after allegedly being beaten in the hills of Teknaf upazila, Cox's Bazar.
Police recovered the bodies from two separate hilly areas of Hnila union yesterday.
According to the officer-in-charge of Teknaf Model Police Station, the killings stemmed from a dispute over a drug consignment.
A survivor, Ilias (35), alleged that the dispute began after 30,000 yaba pills went missing from a hijacked consignment of 1 lakh pills.
He further alleged that they were handed over to an armed drug-trafficking group in the hills of Hnila for punishment over their alleged involvement.
Police have identified several suspects and are currently investigating the incident.
The bodies were sent to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsies.
caption:
Two men were beaten to death in the hills of Teknaf over a dispute involving a hijacked drug consignment.

Two men, identified as Moktar Kamal (48) and Ali Akbar (30), were killed and two others injured after allegedly being beaten in the hills of Teknaf upazila, Cox's Bazar.

Police recovered the bodies from two separate hilly areas of Hnila union yesterday.

According to the officer-in-charge of Teknaf Model Police Station, the killings stemmed from a dispute over a drug consignment.

A survivor, Ilias (35), alleged that the dispute began after 30,000 yaba pills went missing from a hijacked consignment of 1 lakh pills.

He further alleged that they were handed over to an armed drug-trafficking group in the hills of Hnila for punishment over their alleged involvement.

Police have identified several suspects and are currently investigating the incident.

The bodies were sent to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsies.
